_comment: Round 6: the two final-answer variants added in v5 of policies/gdpr-dsar-copy.json (final_gone, final_gone_late; blocks final_open, final_late, final_gone, final_done, final_more) and the new-thread subjects (subjects.new_thread_privacy_erasure, subjects.new_thread_privacy_access), through the gate's own gate.py (check -> pending -> review -> signed statement) in a scratch mirror of this tree, under the gdpr rubric as amended in the same commit (rule 6 exception, rule 8 subjects, the gdpr-final duty). Bodies carry example dates: fixed wording, no personal data. The statements were signed with a THROWAWAY key that exists only in the scratch mirror, so none of these is a verdict the production gate accepts: the verdict a send needs is the one the reviewer host signs on the body node-8 authors after deploy. The mirror differs from the tree in one file, the allowed-signers list. One reviewer pass, 7 bodies, 7 approve.

That completes this request.

If something about you still shows on Muso.AI, reply here with its link and we will look at it.

items.body:
Hello,

The request you made on 11 September 2026 is still open. We are late in answering it, and we are sorry.

What we are doing: your request is open, and we need something from you before we can act on it.

What we need from you:

Before we can act on a Muso page, we need to connect that page to you. Either of these is enough:

1. Claim the page. Sign in to the Muso app (or create an account), open the page and claim it. When the claim has been processed, reply here and we will continue.

2. Reply here with a document from the artist's label or management that names you as authorised to act for the page.

You do not need to send a passport or any other identity document.

When you will hear from us next: by 29 November 2026 at the latest.

Muso.AI Support
